stem:
A 58-year-old woman receives an anticoagulant infusion to treat a pulmonary embolism. The drug is a short-acting agent that, in the body, is stored in mast cells and released when tissues are injured, where it opposes prothrombin.

Which of the following drugs is she receiving?

options.label: A
options.misconception: An oral vitamin K antagonist is being confused with the mast-cell agent.
options.explanation: Warfarin interferes with vitamin K-dependent factor synthesis in the liver and is not stored in mast cells; the endogenous mast-cell anticoagulant is heparin.

options.label: B
options.misconception: An antiplatelet drug is being equated with an anticoagulant.
options.explanation: Aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation rather than the coagulation cascade, and it is not a mast-cell product; the described agent is heparin.

options.label: C
options.misconception: An antifibrinolytic is being presented as an anticoagulant.
options.explanation: Tranexamic acid blocks fibrinolysis and thereby promotes clot stability — the opposite of anticoagulation; the mast-cell anticoagulant described is heparin.

options.label: D
options.misconception: A clot-dissolving enzyme is being confused with a clot-preventing agent.
options.explanation: Streptokinase is a bacterial kinase that activates plasminogen to dissolve existing clots; it neither stores in mast cells nor opposes prothrombin like heparin.

options.label: E
options.misconception: None; heparin is the endogenous mast-cell anticoagulant.
options.explanation: Heparin is a short-acting anticoagulant stored in mast cells and released when tissues are injured, where it opposes prothrombin; it is also used therapeutically and in laboratory samples to prevent clotting.

context: Learning objective: identify endogenous anticoagulants. Heparin is a short-acting anticoagulant stored in mast cells, released upon tissue injury, and acting against prothrombin; it is also the standard anticoagulant for preserving plasma in blood samples, alongside agents such as EDTA.
imageCaption: Hemostasis steps, factor X convergence, fibrin, plasmin fibrinolysis, heparin.
